title: Reconstruction Overdue Draws: Balance-Days over the Charge Span
content:
The balance an overdue draw charge on a Reconstruction contract is figured on follows the charge span and the payments toward the draw. Whichever owed month a charge is for, it is figured on the charge window ending on the charge date. The charge window is 30 days.

**The charge span.** The charge span runs to the charge date from the latest of: the first day of the charge window, which is the 30 days ending on the charge date; the first day a charge may post, which is the day after the grace period's last day; and, when the latest overdue draw charge already posted on the draw was posted on an earlier day, the day after that charge. A payment counts from the day after it is posted.

**The balance.**

- When a payment toward the draw was posted within the past month, the balance is the draw's balance-days over the charge span divided by 30: each day of the span up to and including the latest such payment's posting day counted at the balance before the payments posted within the past month, which is the unpaid amount plus those payments, and each later day at the unpaid amount now.
- When no such payment was posted and the charge span is shorter than the charge window, it is the unpaid amount times the days of the charge span divided by 30.
- Otherwise it is the draw's unpaid amount.

**Counting.** Counting back one month from the charge date, a date is within the past month when it falls after the same day of the month in the previous calendar month and on or before the charge date; when the previous calendar month has no such day, every date in that previous month is outside the past month. Days between two dates are counted as calendar days from the earlier date to the later one, the earlier day not counted; the span's days are its calendar days from its first day through the charge date.

## Grace period by agreement (sets the first day a charge may post)

| Agreement | Grace days after the due date |
|---|---|
| Repair Agreement - Minor Repairs | 5 |
| Standard Rebuild Agreement | 5 |
| Major Rebuild Agreement | 5 |
| Full Structural Rebuild Agreement | 5 |
| Multifamily Unit Rebuild Agreement | 10 |
| Commercial Interior Rebuild Agreement | 10 |

## Worked figures (hypothetical)

A draw due on the 1st of a month on an agreement with a 5-day grace; the charge date is the 20th; no earlier charge on the draw. Grace days run from the 2nd to the 6th, so the span runs from the 7th to the 20th: 14 days.

- **No payment within the past month**, unpaid $4,500.00: the span is shorter than 30 days, so the balance is $4,500.00 times 14 divided by 30, that is $2,100.00.
- **A payment of $1,000.00 posted on the 15th**, unpaid now $3,000.00: the 7th to the 15th, 9 days, count at $4,000.00; the 16th to the 20th, 5 days, at $3,000.00. The balance is 36,000 plus 15,000 balance-days, that is 51,000, divided by 30: $1,700.00.
- **A payment posted on the charge date itself**: every day of the span counts at the balance before the past month's payments.
- **A later charge**: when the previous charge was posted on the 5th of the next month and the charge date is the 25th, the span runs from the 6th to the 25th, 20 days. A second charge posted on the same day as the first does not shorten the span.

Month-end: on a charge date of the 30th of March, a payment posted on the 28th of February is outside the past month, because February has no 30th; a payment on the 1st of March is inside it.
